reason: The first reading gave disconnected letter groups from cut lines; with the Digest text and the printed gloss the line ends and beginnings could be completed, expanded and placed.
sources: Digesta Iustiniani, ed. Th. Mommsen and P. Krueger, D. 4.8.42-52 and 4.9.1-3, transcription at https://www.thelatinlibrary.com/justinian/digest4.shtml

Digestum vetus seu Pandectarum iuris civilis tomus primus ... commentariis Accursii, Paris: G. Merlin, G. Desboys and S. Nivelle, 1566, cols 661-664 (https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_eLlFAAAAcAAJ, leaves n440-n441), page images
text:
F-x60p, source-assisted reading. All lines below were reread on the images by a research reader with the Digest text (Mommsen-Krueger, D. 4.8-4.9) and the printed Accursian gloss (Paris 1566, cols 661-664) at hand; abbreviations are expanded from those sources. Not an independent reading. Accuracy has not been measured.
Conventions: (..) expansion; [..] lost or supplied; ? uncertain; every line is cut at one or both ends. Boxes are native pixels. "recto"/"verso" are the catalogue's canvas labels.
